We advise adding the rope_scaling configuration only when processing long contexts is required. It is also recommended to modify the factor as needed. For example, if the typical context length for your application is 65,536 tokens, it would be better to set factor as 2.0\n\nThe default factor is 4.0, and currently the exllama code will stick to that if the 'default' long context configuration is present: https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/blob/0ff9fd2e39f6307e54358fd1a48a50b5cf7307f8/exllamav3/util/rope.py#L130-L159\n\nBut it *appears* a more optimal thing to do is ignore the rope_scaling factor, and statically set it with `(context length of the loaded model)/original_max_position_embeddings`, which would be 2.0 for 64K, 3.0 for 96K, and so on.\n\nThis is trivially easy to implement, but the question is if exllamav3 should set it automatically like that. *I say* it should, as most users aren't going to dig into how YaRN scaling works and match the scaling factor to their specified context length. \n\n***\n\n...But what would be *even more optimal* would be to dynamically set the scaling factor per request. It flattens all leading logit dimensions into rows, runs the sampling steps and reshapes the selected IDs back to the original leading shape. sequence_ids is accepted but unused here. This is the local interface to generation; tokenizer.actual_vocab_size supplies the boundary for masking padded vocabulary entries.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"SamplingState distinguishes input logits, working logits, weights, normalized probabilities and sorted variants carrying token-index mappings. SS_Sample maps a selected sorted position back through indices[row, position]. These distinctions allow truncation to discard probability mass without requiring immediate renormalization.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"Steps can substitute an alternative and request prerequisites: temperature 1 becomes SS_NoOp, top-k requests sorting, and top-p requests normalized sorted probabilities. However, CustomSampler.__init__ never advances its local state beyond INIT while constructing the list. Prerequisites are therefore chosen conservatively from INIT rather than from the preceding step's output. Runtime normalization and sorting often absorb the redundancy as no-ops; this is not a complete static state-transition planner.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"SS_Temperature divides logits by T, or raises probability weights to 1/T and marks them unnormalized. For positive T these describe the same relative distribution. TopPSampler can apply temperature before truncation, changing which candidates survive, or afterward, changing weights within the retained set. DefaultSampler chooses T=0.75 and top_p=0.75; these are preset choices, with no derivation supplied here. CategoricalSampler maps T=0 to greedy selection; TopKSampler also does so for k=1, and TopPSampler for p=0.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"Top-k keeps the first k sorted entries, replacing the rest with zero weights or negative-infinity logits; it uses a full sort rather than a partial top-k operation. Top-p computes inclusive cumulative probabilities and keeps entries whose cumulative sum is at most p, except that the first entry is always preserved. Thus it excludes the entry that first crosses the threshold, rather than retaining the smallest prefix reaching p. Top-k requires k>=1; SS_TopP requires 0<p<=1.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"A scalar translation confirmed this top-p boundary: weights [0.5, 0.3125, 0.1875] at p=0.75 become [0.5, 0, 0]. The second entry would cross to 0.8125 and is removed. The example uses exactly representable binary fractions, avoiding ambiguity from a cumulative-sum rounding boundary.\", \"basis\": \"execution\"}, {\"text\": \"Token restrictions precede the sampling chain. Vocabulary padding is masked in the caller's logits in place; blocked/allowed filtering subsequently clones the tensor. Blocked IDs receive negative infinity, while an allowed list masks every ID outside that list. Applying both therefore retains allowed IDs minus blocked IDs. No local check prevents an empty candidate set. If no seed is supplied, Python chooses an integer in [0, 2^32-1]; an explicit seed also resets the global Python and Torch random generators.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"SS_Sample implements perturb-and-argmax: input logits use gumbel_noise_f16, working logits use gumbel_noise_f32, and probability weights use gumbel_noise_log, which takes their logarithm before adding noise. The latter two overwrite their working buffers. In ideal arithmetic, argmax(log(w_i)+G_i), with independent standard Gumbel noise, samples proportionally to positive weights w_i. Normalizing weights only adds a common offset to those scores, explaining why sampling can follow truncation without another normalization pass; zero weights become negative infinity.\", \"basis\": \"inference\"}, {\"text\": \"The CUDA Gumbel transform is -log(max(-log(max(u, 1e-20)), 1e-20)). The two 1e-20 guards prevent logarithms of zero at either endpoint; they are numerical guards, not filtering thresholds. Noise kernels initialize Philox using the supplied seed and flattened element index. FP32 kernels process one value per thread; FP16 processes half2 pairs, adds noise in float, then rounds back to half. Consequently, the unmodified-temperature FP16 route is not numerically identical to the FP32 working-logit route.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"Binary64 evaluation of the guarded transform gives approximately -3.82976472 at u=0 and 46.05170186 at u=1. Their wrappers require two-dimensional half logits and long output tensors, and clamp max_logit to the stored width; zero means the full width. They run on the current CUDA stream. In contrast, CustomSampler materializes noisy values and delegates selection to torch.argmax. Fusion avoids that intermediate noise-output pass, but no speed advantage was measured.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"The fused Gumbel kernel seeds Philox with threadIdx.x but not blockIdx.x, so rows reuse the same per-thread noise streams for a given seed. It also differs from the standalone noise kernels' per-element initialization. Its read2f boundary checks are reversed for an odd max_logit: the low lane tests idx<max_logit-1, while the high lane tests idx<max_logit. Neither this reader nor the FP16 noise kernel guards the second lane of an odd-sized half2 tail.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"Scalar evaluation of read2f's masks with six stored logits and max_logit=5 admitted indices [0,1,2,3,5], excluding valid index 4 and admitting padded index 5. This demonstrates the predicate issue without executing a native memory access.\", \"basis\": \"execution\"}, {\"text\": \"Generic greedy composition has a separate defect: SS_Argmax's sorted branches assign the indexed result to state.state instead of state.sample, then overwrite state.state with DONE. Plain ArgmaxSampler starts at INIT and does not exercise those branches.\", \"basis\": \"source\"}, {\"text\": \"partial_strings_match consumes byte buffers containing UTF-32 query text, packed patterns and byte offsets; dividing by four yields codepoint lengths and offsets. It scans patterns in list order, returning a full-match start index, -2 for a query suffix matching a pattern prefix, or -1 for no match.
